accueil.titre: Maryse's cooking notebook, for busy weeks
accueil.intro: Between her job and a big tennis club where she is general secretary, Maryse has no time to waste. Her notebook sorts out the week's meals in a few minutes: tried-and-tested recipes, a planned menu, a shopping list that writes itself. Here it is, in your pocket.
accueil.photoNote: The day I got my medal. My colleagues told me: “Your notebook, turn it into an app!”
accueil.contenuTitre: Three pages that save you time
accueil.recettesTexte: Your notebook starts with 20 of Maryse's recipes, tried and approved. Copy the ones you like, add your own, find them by how much time you have.
accueil.planningTexte: Lunch and dinner, Monday to Sunday: drop a recipe onto a meal, like pinning a note on the fridge. The whole week is sorted in one go.
accueil.coursesTexte: One click and the week's ingredients are gathered, quantities added up. One list, one trip to the shop.
accueil.citation: “At the club, nothing happens without a schedule. I didn't see why meals should be any different.”
accueil.finTexte: Create your account in a minute: Maryse's recipes are already inside. The time you save is yours to spend as you like.

histoire.intro: Maryse & Co was born from a squared school notebook, a packed diary and a medal ceremony.
histoire.fiction: A story inspired by Maryse, partly imagined for this demo.

etapes.titre: The office, the club, and everything else
etapes.texte: Maryse runs her career and, alongside it, the general secretariat of a big tennis club: general meetings, tournaments, memberships, volunteers to coordinate. Her weeks are full, and every minute counts.

She applies the method that works at the club to meals: write everything down, plan everything. In a school notebook, the tried-and-tested recipes, the week's menu on the back, the shopping list on the last page. Ten minutes on Sunday, and the week is sorted.
When Maryse receives her Medal of Honour for Labour, her colleagues give her flowers and some advice: that notebook everyone keeps borrowing, at the office and at the club, should be shared.
The notebook becomes an online notebook. Same recipes, same method, and room for yours.

histoire.fin: And you, what will you do with the time you save?

sections.texte: Maryse & Co is a technical demo project with no commercial activity, published from a public GitHub repository.

The site is hosted by GitHub Pages (GitHub Inc., 88 Colin P. Kelly Jr. Street, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA). Accounts and notebook data are hosted by Supabase Inc., on servers located in the European Union.
The photographs of Maryse are published with the consent of the people shown. Any reuse is forbidden.
For any question, open an issue on the project's GitHub repository.
Your email address, your first name, your preferences (language, theme) and what you write in the notebook: recipes, meal plan and shopping list.
Only to make your notebook work: signing you in and giving you back your data. No ads, no resale, no audience measurement tools.
Nobody but you. Data is protected row by row in the database: an account can only read its own information.
At Supabase, in the European Union. Your language and theme are also remembered in your browser (local storage), with no advertising cookies.
As long as your account exists. Since this site is a demo, inactive accounts may be deleted.
You can ask to access, correct or delete your data by opening an issue on the project's GitHub repository. You can also lodge a complaint with the CNIL, the French data protection authority.

evenement.intro: On 7 November 2026, it's the semi-final of the Challenge mixte de l'Isère! To be in top shape on the big day, here are a few simple recipes to make before, during and after the match.

recettes.titre: Wholewheat pasta with chicken and vegetables
recettes.description: Pasta to fill up on energy, without a heavy evening.
etapes: Dice the chicken and cut the vegetables into small pieces.
Soften the onion in the olive oil, add the chicken and let it brown for 5 minutes.
Add the courgette and pepper, cover and cook for 10 minutes over a low heat.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta. Drain it and mix it with the vegetables. Season with salt and pepper.

recettes.moment: On the morning of the match
recettes.description: A breakfast that is gentle on the stomach, to eat about three hours before the match.
etapes: Put the oats and milk in a saucepan.
Heat gently for 5 minutes, stirring, until creamy.
Add the sliced banana, the honey and the cinnamon. Eat warm.

recettes.titre: Homemade cereal bars with dried fruit
recettes.description: To slip into your bag for a snack during the day or on the way home.
etapes: Chop the apricots and roughly crush the almonds. Mix them with the oats and raisins.
Melt the butter with the honey. Pour over the mixture, add the beaten egg and mix well.
Press the mixture into a tin lined with baking paper and bake for 20 minutes. Let it cool before cutting into bars.

recettes.titre: Rice bowl with soft-boiled egg and vegetables
recettes.description: A complete, colourful meal to recover well.
etapes: Cut the broccoli into small florets and steam for 5 minutes. Grate the carrots.
Lower the eggs into boiling water for 6 minutes, then into cold water, and peel them.
Share the rice between the bowls, add the vegetables and the halved eggs. Drizzle with soy sauce and sprinkle with sesame.

recettes.description: To quench your thirst and treat yourself when you get home.
etapes: Hull the strawberries and cut the banana into pieces.
Serve straight away, nice and cold.

evenement.avertissement: These recipes are simple ideas for eating well around the match, not a training plan. If you follow a special diet, ask a health professional for advice.
evenement.finTitre: Want to keep them close at hand?
evenement.finTexte: Start your notebook: you can write these recipes down and drop them into your weekly menu.
